newsitem.title: USA: Sharp U.S. spot prod gains continue into close.
newsitem.headline: Sharp U.S. spot prod gains continue into close.

text.p: U.S. spot refined product prices continued to move higher at mid-afternoon Wednesday, led by the jump in NYMEX prices and the gains in Gulf gasoline differentials.

Traders said prompt U.S. Gulf regular M4 conventional unleaded traded at 4.00 cents over December NYMEX, up about 1.25 cents from its early afternoon level. Offers stood at about 4.50 cents above the NYMEX price. Activity in Houston was brisk, with an estimated 200,000 barrels changing hands.
Market players were extremely busy assessing the cash market's response to the sharp NYMEX moves in both gasoline and heating oil, and liquidity appeared to be light.

"It's a little bit of an impediment to buying. The 'Merc' took us out of the action early," one trader in Houston said, noting differential movement is of secondary importance during such a sharp NYMEX move.
"If the dog's moved that much, it doesn't matter where the fleas are going," he added.
Heating oil differentials in Houston and in New York Harbor appeared to be holding steady, but some players said the cash markets were beginning to echo the strength on the NYMEX.
-- Matt Daily New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1828
